messages:
olivia: quick heads-up — we started seeing tail latency regressions on small-prompt traffic after yesterday's cohort allocator tweak. short prompts (<=16 tokens) now have p99 ~ 320ms up from ~180ms. suspecting KV cache churn when we aggregate short + medium prompts into the same continuous batch cohort.
raj: can you paste the perf slice / profile? is it kernel scheduling or cache misses?
olivia: pasted a short excerpt from flame:
```
pprof flame: cpu
p99 latency jumps map to repeated kv-lookup hotpaths (kv_get -> kv_evict) during steady-state burst
stack: serve.go:312 -> cohort_alloc.go:78 -> kv_cache.go:145
```
cheng: I ran a lightweight trace on the canary node, here's the sampling output (trimmed):
- requests: 12k over 10m
- kv hit-rate overall: 72%
- kv hit-rate short-prompts: 38%
- avg batch size short-prompts: 6
- decode-rate short-prompts: ~60 tokens/s (fast)
looks like short prompts are thrashing the prefix cache because they get interleaved with longer decode-rate sessions.
raj: that matches my hypothesis. when short fast-decoding streams share a batch with slow long-decoding ones, the runtime swaps KV contexts more frequently and we lose prefix reuse.
olivia: thinking config levers: 1) separate decode-rate cohorts (fast vs slow) in addition to length buckets, 2) reduce per-request token_budget for cohorts dominated by short prompts (lower prefetched tokens), 3) bias admission policy to prefer homogeneous batches for KV locality.
cheng: +1. quick config suggestion (cohort allocator snippet):
```json
{
  "cohort_rules": [
    {"name": "short-fast", "length_max": 16, "decode_rate_max": 80, "token_budget": 32},
    {"name": "short-slow", "length_max": 16, "decode_rate_min": 81, "token_budget": 64},
    {"name": "long", "length_min": 17, "token_budget": 128}
  ]
}
```
raj: can we avoid a huge rollout? suggest canary to 5% of short-prompt traffic with realtime kv_hit_rate and p99_latency dashboards. also capture batch homogeneity metric (entropy of lengths/decode rates per batch).
olivia: agreed. I'll wire a quick dashboard panel: kv_hit_rate_by_cohort, p99_latency_by_cohort, batch_entropy. I'll also add an alert if short-fast kv_hit_rate < 50% or p99 > 250ms.
infra-bot: deploy requested by olivia:cohort-tune-2026. canary=5% namespace=canary-2. image=serve:v2026.03.15-olivia-cohort.
cheng: after applying the cohort split in canary, measured kv_hit_rate short-fast -> 68% and p99 down to 190ms within 30m. batch_entropy fell from 1.2 -> 0.4 (good).
raj: nice numbers. any regressions on long prompts?
cheng: long cohort stable, p99 unchanged. we should still monitor cost since smaller token_budget may increase decode re-compute for longer sequences if misclassified.
olivia: plan: keep canary for 6h, then ramp to 25% if no alerts. I'll open an RFC with config defaults and a migration note for Dedicated customers (they can opt-in).
raj: please include a short perf test script so QA can reproduce — include a mix of short-fast and long-slow traffic and a script to compute batch entropy + kv hit rate.
olivia: will do. thanks all :tada:
cheng: putting the trace and raw samples in the infra bucket: gs://redwood-perf/cohort-tune/1761112223/samples.tar.gz
olivia: filing follow-ups: 1) RFC, 2) QA perf script, 3) rollout plan w/ dashboards. will update thread when canary hits 25%.
raj: ack, and please ping me before ramp.
infra-bot: canary rollout started: cohort-tune-2026 -> canary-2 at 5% (1761112388)
